name: Treviso Airport
before:
Sold by some airlines as Venice-Treviso, and that is the thing to be straight with a client about. The airport is 3 km from Treviso and about 31 km from Venice, and Venice's own airport is Marco Polo. It is used mainly by low cost carriers, and Ryanair opened a base here in December 2020 with eighteen new routes.

Getting to Venice is well organised, but it is a transfer. Barzi Bus Service runs a coach timed to Ryanair and Wizz Air flights that reaches Venice in forty minutes by motorway, and since October 2024 a Flibco shuttle has run up to fifteen times a day to Mestre station and Venezia Tronchetto. For Treviso itself a Mobilità di Marca public bus runs to Treviso Centrale station. There is also a daily coach to Ljubljana.

The terminal opened in 2007 and is named after the sculptor Antonio Canova. The runway is 2,420 metres. Parking runs to 564 long stay spaces and 50 short stay in front of the building.
after:
Sold by some airlines as Venice-Treviso, and that is the thing to be straight with a client about. The airport is a few kilometres south west of Treviso and about 31 km from Venice, and Venice's own airport is Marco Polo. Ryanair flies here, though its own airport data does not list Treviso as a base.

Getting to Venice is well organised, but it is a transfer. Barzi Service runs a coach about once an hour to Mestre station and Venezia Tronchetto, reaching Venice in about 40 minutes by motorway. For Treviso itself a Mobilità di Marca bus runs to Treviso Centrale station.

The airport is named after the sculptor Antonio Canova. Its runway is 2,420 metres.
